Frequently asked questions

How do I move around the 3D model?

Rotate: drag with one finger (or the mouse). Zoom: pinch (or scroll). Pan: drag with two fingers (or right-click and drag).

Use the front, back and side view buttons to snap to a standard angle.

How do I focus on a single organ or structure?

Pick a category such as Heart, Brain or Lungs from the category strip, then tap any structure to select it. Use Isolate to hide everything else, and the exploded layout to separate the pieces.

You can also search for a structure by name within the current category.

How do I show or hide body systems and layers?

Open the layers panel and toggle individual systems on or off. The heart view adds chamber, valve, wall and vessel layers, plus a Reveal inside option.

The model is blank or loading slowly. What can I do?

The anatomy data is detailed and may take a moment to load the first time, especially on a slow connection. If the model doesn't appear:

  • Check your internet connection and reopen the app.
  • Make sure your device is running the latest version of iOS / iPadOS.
  • Close other apps to free up memory, then try again.

If the problem continues, email us with your device model and OS version.

Why do some organs have only one piece?

Some small organs, such as the stomach and spleen, are modeled as a single mesh in the source dataset, so they can't be broken down further. Counts shown in each category are modeled pieces, not distinct organs.

Can I use Human Atlas for medical diagnosis?

No. Human Atlas is for education and exploration only. It shows an adult male reference anatomy and does not represent all anatomical variation. Colors and exploded positions are for clarity and do not simulate physiology. Always consult a qualified medical professional for health decisions.

Do I need an account? What data do you collect?

No account is required. Human Atlas does not ask for personal information and does not include advertising or analytics tracking.

Reporting a problem

To help us fix issues quickly, please include:

  • Your device model (e.g. iPhone 15, iPad Air)
  • Your iOS / iPadOS version
  • Which category or structure you were viewing
  • What happened, and a screenshot if possible
